cohort: The study included 1163 children with prelingually sensorineural deafness (PLSND), 15% of whom exhibited cerebral white matter lesions (CWMLs), who underwent cochlear implantation.
finding: Greater severity of cerebral white matter lesions (CWMLs) and elevated pre-CI hearing thresholds are risk factors for poorer post-cochlear implantation (CI) auditory and speech outcomes, while CWMLs severity also independently predicted poorer post-CI non-verbal cognitive (NVC) outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was identified as a protective factor for post-CI auditory, speech, and non-verbal cognitive outcomes.
